name: Lefferts Historic House

dates.built: 1777 (the survey's own figure: 'Rebuilt after fire of 1776, in 1777')
dates.note: The survey states two: 'Date of Erection Original house--latter part of the l?th century. Rebuilt after fire of 1776, in 1777', and later 'Using the old foundation, timbers and unburaed portions of the original house, Pieter Lefferts and a few skilled carpenters built the present homestead in 1777.' Wikipedia and the Historic House Trust give 'circa 1783'. Both are on the record; neither is edited.
dates.altered: The survey: 'Wood dormers, porch and columns added and alterations made in the interior in 1855, hut no changes were made when moved in 1917'. Moved six blocks from 563 Flatbush Avenue into Prospect Park in 1918 (Wikipedia; the survey says 1917 and states the cost as $16,000). The 1850s rear wing was removed at the move.

quotes.text: The Lefferts Homestead as it stands today represents a type as developed in this locality in the 18th century. It was considered of historic importance and fine enough example of type by the City of Hew York to preserve and place in Prospect Park.

note: Tranche 2, the Dutch trunk in America. Added by this pass to give `dutch-colonial-american` its Long Island frame-and-shingle gambrel beside the stone houses. THE MATERIALS LINE IS THE FINDING: 'Masonry foundation, wood floors, wood walls, shingle sides and roof' -- a wholly timber house of the same culture whose Hudson branch the node describes as twenty to thirty inches of stone. The node's own prose says the walls follow the geology, and this record is the Long Island end of that sentence. Note also that the survey records the DORMERS AND THE PORCH AS 1855 ADDITIONS, which matters before anyone reads a photograph of this house as evidence about either.
